## CONVERGING contract — integrated implementation baseline

This document is the single target authority for diagram composition and
certified authoring/compiled projections. Common circuit assembly is owned by
the [assembly contract](circuit-plan-assembly.qmd). The implementation baseline
is integrated, but this scope is not Human-accepted or stabilized. The
[central evidence status](index.qmd#implementation-evidence-status) bounds
current execution and delivery claims.

Accepted numerical operations, physical component models, units,
workspace evidence, and Result meanings remain authoritative and are not
redefined here. No compatibility path from the frozen flat-node or
catalog-hint candidates is promised.
:::

## Product promise

An author declares each physical component, electrical connection, ownership
boundary, and structural role once. Numerical compilation and diagram
projection consume that same declaration:

```text
Library component facts
          |
          v
CircuitPlan + inline SubsystemPlan + reusable CompositePlan
          |
          +----> numerical lowering and existing Run/Result evidence
          |
          +----> authoring or compiled certified diagram
```

The diagram never supplies topology to the solver. The solver never infers
authoring intent from component names, a drawing, or incidental graph shape.

This contract owns:

- diagram-only Block and wiring composition over authored handles;
- authoring and compiled projection evidence;
- diagram evidence and presentation identities, referencing the shared Plan
  identity without redefining it; and
- layout and audit failure behavior.

The [Component Authoring Contract](../component-authoring.qmd) retains physical
factory values, component schemas, RLGC, Josephson, SQUID, mutual-inductance,
and backend-realization authority. The
[V1 Runtime Contract](../v1-runtime-contract.qmd) retains execution, view,
request, workspace, Result, and report authority.

## Shared assembly authority

The [CircuitPlan Assembly Contract](circuit-plan-assembly.qmd) owns the common
electrical grammar, three assembly scopes, public boundaries, completeness,
and Plan identity. This document consumes that immutable declaration; it does
not own assembly or require rendering for Parameter or Calculation use.

### Canonical-ground visual grammar {#native-branches-and-ground}

Native R/L/C/JJ branches are visible electrical symbols. Local ground
occurrences derive from authored structural terminations, never one scope-wide
ground tree. A Parallel's shared grounded end rail has one ground glyph;
separate grounded shunts each retain their own local glyph, including the two
shunts of a floating network. Their default presentation is outward from the
owning structure. `composition.ground_side(...)` controls a grounded
structure's termination side, rotating the structure when necessary without
reversing its electrical reference or creating a ground domain. Eligible
parent-applied ground pins retain parent-side presentation, and Port loads
retain their own graphical role. Several glyphs may denote the same canonical
reference; their placement or call grouping does not create distinct
electrical grounds. N-link geometry is shared and drawn once rather
than as duplicate pairwise wires. A continuous bus or link is conductive.
Ownership regions, labels, guides, and provenance panels are nonconductive and
must not look like wires or junction dots.

Only transmission-line and multi-conductor-line bodies may use an electrical
box with a complete pin/conductor legend. Ordinary C/L/JJ networks remain
expanded native symbols; a Subsystem box never hides their topology.

For an N=1 CPW, the authoring Box instead uses the compact two-endpoint
grammar: kind/local ID, effective length when values are enabled, and captured
occurrence `n_sections` always, visibly written as `1 section` or `<N> sections`.
Conductor, reference, and head/tail names are
not drawn. The two visible endpoints compare without claiming ordered
head/tail identity; exact endpoint identity and RLGC remain source-verified.
MTL retains the necessary ordered conductor and terminal evidence. Compiled
scientific evidence is unchanged.

Authoring scalar labels use Decimal `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` to six significant
digits, removing trailing zeros. Dimensionful quantities use supported
engineering SI prefixes with `1 <= abs(mantissa) < 1000`, including a carry
to the next prefix after rounding. Zero is explicit, negative signs remain,
and dimensionless values have no prefix. Values outside the supported prefix
range use scientific notation rather than truncating to zero. This display
rule covers physical values, length, Port reference impedance, and coupling
coefficient; exact model, source, parameter, and request values do not change.

## Diagram request and composition {#schematic-layout}

The target keeps one diagram request:

```python
CircuitDiagramSpec(
    representation="authoring",
    theme=Theme.AUTO,
    show_parameter_values=True,
    show_provenance=True,
    layout=None,
)
```

Its exact target signature and Plan operation are:

```text
CircuitDiagramSpec(
    *, representation: Literal["authoring", "compiled"] = "authoring",
    theme: Theme = Theme.AUTO,
    show_parameter_values: bool = True,
    show_provenance: bool = True,
    layout: SchematicComposition | SchematicLayout | None = None,
) -> CircuitDiagramSpec
CircuitPlan.render_schematic(
    spec: CircuitDiagramSpec = CircuitDiagramSpec(),
    *, parameters: ParameterSet | None = None,
) -> CircuitDiagramResult
```

`representation` selects the original structured-authoring projection or the
compiler-expanded projection. It cannot select a reduced View, transformed
coordinate system, `ParameterSpace`, PTC result, or solver Result. The optional
single `ParameterSet` selects physical values for that projection; it is not a
View or an optimizer-candidate lookup.

Composition and layout hints apply only to the authoring projection. A compiled
request with a non-`None` layout rejects with
`SCNSimValidationError(stage="schematic_layout")`; compiled matrix-stamp
projection and its evidence are unchanged.

### One public composition path {#schematic-composition}

`SchematicComposition(plan=plan)`, `SchematicComposition.automatic(plan=plan,
hints=None)`, and `layout=None` share one fixed Default completion flow. The
constructor permits a partial configuration: explicit per-field choices win,
and omitted fields receive stable defaults. There is no separate whole-manual
completeness mode. `SchematicLayout` supplies its existing optional hints to
this same flow. `show()` and inventory/wiring reads are nonmutating and may
distinguish explicit settings from fields awaiting Default completion.

A Block is an existing scope peer or assembly structure, not a new component,
ownership boundary, or electrical declaration. Built-Composite internals remain
nonaddressable to callers. Default uses the same public builders as explicit
composition; it does not rank alternatives or search for a preferred recipe.
There is no global reset-to-auto, coordinate, length, size, or gap API.

Replacing wiring is different from omitting a setting: `replace_wiring()`
replaces one complete owner-local group. Its edited attachments and arms may
be temporarily incomplete, but capture rejects missing connections. Default
never guesses missing wires in an explicit replacement.

The public setting operations use the existing typed handles and strict
`DiagramAxis` / `DiagramSide` enums:

```text
composition.axis(block, axis)
composition.order(scope_or_parallel, members=(...))
composition.terminal_side(pin_or_tap, side)
composition.port_side(port, side)
composition.port_orientation(port, *, boundary_side=..., load_side=...)
composition.tap_order(bus, taps=(...))
composition.ground_side(grounded_structure_or_eligible_parent_ground_pin, side)
```

These operations configure presentation, never component contents, ownership,
ordered model endpoints, or connectivity. There are no public coordinates,
line lengths, sizes, or spacing controls. A setting within an inline scope
configures that scope; a parent cannot address child-private internals. Complete
local orders preserve the existing ownership and member boundaries:
`order(scope, members=...)` includes only its independent complete component
peers and child regions, while `order(parallel, members=...)` includes its
complete branch collection. Connector structures are placed through their
declared endpoints, not added to the scope peer permutation. Block inventory
does include those structures for axis and endpoint selection.
`composition.axis(...)` also accepts a complete `ComponentInstance` Block;
the existing five-map convenience retains its narrower eligible handle types.
Private Series midpoints and Parallel rails remain inside their structures.

`port_orientation()` sets two perpendicular `DiagramSide` directions in the
root frame, giving eight poses. `boundary_side` is the hollow marker's side;
`load_side` points from the internal T toward the load and ground. The complete
setter replaces both atomically. `port_side()` changes only the boundary side
in that same state, preserves an explicit load side, and atomically rejects an
incompatible change. `ground_side()` does not accept a Port. Each Port is one
complete measured Block with its T, marker, load, ground, labels, and circuit
lead. Its external attachment is the circuit-facing lead end, not its hollow
marker, ground, or internal center.

| Boundary side | Perpendicular load-side choices |
|---|---|
| `LEFT` | `TOP`, `BOTTOM` |
| `RIGHT` | `TOP`, `BOTTOM` |
| `TOP` | `LEFT`, `RIGHT` |
| `BOTTOM` | `LEFT`, `RIGHT` |

A `SeriesRef` generated as a Parallel branch shares its containing Parallel's
orientation; it is not an independently rotatable Block. An axis constraint
on that branch, including one supplied through `SchematicLayout.axes`, is a
redundant constraint checked at capture against the Parallel's effective axis.
An equal axis succeeds; a conflicting axis rejects with the branch and
Parallel IDs. Setter order does not select a winning orientation.

A composition binds the exact Plan captured at construction. Updating that
Plan makes the old composition stale rather than silently rebuilding it. Render
captures one `AuthoringSnapshot`, its effective `ResolvedPlanPoint`, display
settings, and font environment. One isolated Default completion supplies one
measured body per child, one constructive placement, and one fixed routing
realization. Success and failure leave caller state and refs unchanged. The
completed recipe and the same verified scene are frozen together; later recipe edits cannot change an existing
`CircuitDiagramResult` or its Drawing, SVG, or Notebook presentation.

### Attachments and owner-local wiring {#composition-wiring}

Signal wiring groups follow owner-local Bus/Tap relations, Links,
exposure/backing relations, and structural boundary incidence. Grouping does
not cross a child or any physical body. Two external groups can therefore
share one global electrical node through genuine child wiring while remaining
independently editable. A coupling ending at `plus_1` and a probe-side Link
from intrinsically equivalent `plus_2` are distinct parent-local groups.
Canonical ground does not merge these groups; ground presentation stays local.

Every public boundary and its side target remains visible, including open
boundaries. An unused pin contributes no imaginary outward Parent wire.
Only actual outward incidence enters a parent wiring inventory. A Port belongs
to the local class of its unique root Bus, never an arbitrary same-net group.
The child's entire internal measured drawing remains child-owned; the parent
only translates it whole. Electrical witness A observes real continuity,
structural witness B observes named boundaries and ownership, and composition
conformance checks the corresponding local visible wire component without
claiming wires from a sibling group.

`composition.endpoint(ref, boundary=...)` returns a typed presentation
attachment, not an `ElectricNodeRef` or `CoordinateRef`. A structure selects
its explicit `"start"` or `"end"` boundary; a Branch selects `"at"` or
`"end"`. A public Pin, logical Port, or authored Tap selects its existing
attachment without a structure-boundary selector. Two structures sharing a
Bus still have distinct boundary attachments. Aliases of one actual attachment
normalize to that attachment; the Bus itself is not an additional junction arm.

`composition.replace_wiring(at=bus_or_link_or_public_pin)` selects one
owner-local inter-Block wiring group. A Subsystem public Pin selects its
parent-facing incidence; a ComponentInstance public Pin selects incidence in
the occurrence's owning scope. Neither selects child-private wiring or falls
back to the child's internal side. No legal outward group means failure.
`endpoint(pin)` resolves within the selected group. An ambiguous Tap requires
an explicit structure boundary; it never selects the first or unused contact
or creates another arm. Bus, Link, and Pin aliases only within the same local
class share one
replacement authority. Its complete attachment inventory comes from all
authored relations, not the number of endpoints in a selected `link()` call.
Replacing a group clears its previous wiring and invalidates its old wiring
refs so they cannot create a competing recipe. General replacement rejects
ground networks; their per-structure graphical roles remain separate.

The returned wiring group exposes:

```text
wiring.straight(id=..., axis=DiagramAxis...)
wiring.elbow(id=..., sides=(adjacent sides))
wiring.tee(id=..., branch=DiagramSide...)
wiring.cross(id=...)
wiring.connect(a, b)
```

Each requested primitive has only its eligible `.left`, `.right`, `.top`,
and `.bottom` arm refs. Straight has two opposite arms along its axis; an
elbow has its two adjacent arms; a tee has the selected branch and its
perpendicular through-arms; a cross has all four arms at one junction. These
are local conductive arm patterns, not new electrical elements, nets, taps, or
analysis coordinates. Every external attachment and every requested arm must
be connected exactly once, and all members of the group must be connected.
Duplicate, missing, foreign-net, foreign-group, invalid-side, invalid-shape,
and stale refs reject; an incomplete edited group cannot render.

`connect()` may add route elbows needed to avoid obstacles, using the same
straight/L primitive machinery and preserving the requested arm directions.
It cannot replace a requested Cross with two Ts, even though those alternatives
could express the same electrical node. Shape verification checks the actual
visible arm geometry separately from electrical witness A and ownership
witness B. Passing A/B cannot excuse a different requested composition. T/Cross
sides constrain local arms, not a global half-plane for distant Blocks;
necessary elbows remain legal without turning a chosen arm into a huge detour.

The capstone can replace one root group without changing its four Ports,
physical model, or numerical requests. The named handles below are from its
completed feedline/readout/floating declaration:

```python
composition = SchematicComposition.automatic(plan=plan)
wiring = composition.replace_wiring(at=readout_root_bus)
readout_t = wiring.tee(id="readout_attachment", branch=DiagramSide.BOTTOM)
split_t = wiring.tee(id="floating_split", branch=DiagramSide.BOTTOM)
lower_turn = wiring.elbow(id="floating_minus_turn", sides=(DiagramSide.TOP, DiagramSide.RIGHT))
wiring.connect(composition.endpoint(feedline_readout, boundary="end"), readout_t.left)
wiring.connect(readout_t.bottom, composition.endpoint(readout_terminal))
wiring.connect(readout_t.right, split_t.left)
wiring.connect(split_t.right, composition.endpoint(readout_floating_plus, boundary="start"))
wiring.connect(split_t.bottom, lower_turn.top)
wiring.connect(lower_turn.right, composition.endpoint(readout_floating_minus, boundary="start"))
diagram = plan.render_schematic(CircuitDiagramSpec(layout=composition))
```

### SchematicLayout convenience

`SchematicLayout` is immutable and defensively copies five optional mappings.
Its mappings are converted into the corresponding public composition setting
operations, then fixed Default completes omitted fields at render.
The target type shape below
is contract notation, not executable Python:

```text
SchematicLayout(
    *,
    axes: Mapping[
        CircuitPlan | SubsystemPlan |
        SeriesRef | ParallelRef | BranchRef,
        DiagramAxis,
    ] = {},
    order: Mapping[
        CircuitPlan | SubsystemPlan | ParallelRef,
        tuple[ComponentInstance | SubsystemPlan | SeriesRef, ...],
    ] = {},
    terminal_sides: Mapping[PinRef | TapRef, DiagramSide] = {},
    port_sides: Mapping[PortRef, DiagramSide] = {},
    tap_order: Mapping[BusRef, tuple[TapRef, ...]] = {},
) -> SchematicLayout
```

`DiagramAxis` accepts only `HORIZONTAL` or `VERTICAL`; `DiagramSide` accepts
only `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `TOP`, or `BOTTOM`. Both are strict string Enums and raw
strings raise `TypeError`.

- `axes` orients the rendered root `CircuitPlan`, an attached live inline
  `SubsystemPlan`, or a structured group. Rendering belongs only to
  `CircuitPlan`; a detached `CompositePlan` and private scopes inside a built
  Composite are not layout keys.
- For a scope key, `order` is a complete permutation of its direct peer
  `ComponentInstance` and `SubsystemPlan` handles. This includes a complete
  Composite occurrence or native multi-terminal body that remains independent.
  A component body already consumed by a series, parallel, or branch structure
  is not a peer; neither are buses, taps, Ports, or connector structures. The
  value must list every eligible peer exactly once—omission is a validation
  failure, not a partial hint. For a `ParallelRef` key, the value is exactly a
  complete permutation of its `.branches` `SeriesRef`s. Key-dependent
  validation rejects every other mixture. Electrical members inside a
  `SeriesRef` cannot be reordered.
- `terminal_sides` constrains public boundary pins or declared bus taps owned
  by the referenced scope.
- `port_sides` constrains root `PortRef`s.
- `tap_order` gives the relative geometric order of explicitly named taps on
  one authored bus. A key is a live root or inline-Subsystem `BusRef` in the
  rendered Plan, including an electrically private bus in either eligible
  scope. Layout-key eligibility does not publish electrical or analytical
  access. Its value is a complete permutation of that exact bus's declared
  `TapRef`s; an empty tuple is harmless only when the bus has no declared taps.
  Private buses inside a built Composite remain inaccessible.

`tap_order` binds the exact authored `BusRef` and its owner-region segment, not
canonical electrical-node identity. Parent and child buses joined by a public
pin therefore keep separate local order frames. Along the bus owner's effective
local axis, the listed named taps have strictly increasing projected
contact-anchor positions: left to right for `HORIZONTAL` and top to bottom for
`VERTICAL`. Axes on incident `SeriesRef`, `ParallelRef`, or `BranchRef` objects
do not redefine that frame. Implicit direct-bus contacts are renderer
bookkeeping, not public refs, and may automatically precede, interleave with,
or follow the named taps. The complete tuple orders only the named taps
relative to one another.

The mapping does not define current flow, series order, node order, a new tap,
or a connection. Default tap placement follows connected structure and other
eligible layout constraints; `.tap()` call order and words such as `left` or
`right` do not command geometry. Side constraints and `tap_order` are
conjoined; neither silently overrides the other. A raw string or any other
wrong key or value type raises `TypeError`. A well-typed stale, foreign, or
hidden bus or tap, a missing, duplicate, or other-bus tap, an incomplete
permutation, or an incompatible or otherwise conflicting hint raises
`SCNSimValidationError(stage="schematic_layout")`. Both failure classes reject
the request before a Result, workspace, or partial image exists.

Changing only `tap_order`, another layout mapping, or Theme preserves Plan,
connectivity, and semantic digests. Adding or removing an authored tap changes
the structural declaration and need not preserve Plan or semantic identity,
even when the electrical net is equivalent. A/B correspondence checks visible
electrical and ownership incidence; separate layout validation checks requested
geometry where the attachment rays are unambiguous. An ambiguous
multi-incidence Tap does not provide an independent exact Tap-name-to-picture
observation. Its authored Tap identity remains verified source evidence, not a
hidden label that the witness claims to recover from the image.

Foreign, hidden, dead, duplicate, missing, or conflicting handles fail closed.
The refs bind live authoring ownership captured at render. Editing a mutable
unsealed Plan and rendering again captures the new declaration; there is no
pre-render catalog, public ref constructor, stale snapshot ceremony, or raw
coordinate override.

### Fixed Default layout and ownership regions

Default resolves explicit `series`, `parallel`, `branch`, `bus`, `tap`,
coupling, and scope facts once. It neither infers intent from names/Port roles
nor creates a second authoring engine. Default and explicit composition use the
same Block, attachment, straight/L/T/Cross, native measurement, and validation
machinery.

Two attachments use a straight or L; three use a T with exactly compatible
directions where available, otherwise its fixed scope branch (bottom for a
horizontal scope, right for a vertical one). Four all-distinct directions use
a Cross; other four-contact groups use connected Ts. Larger groups use a fixed
T chain along the scope axis. Exact compatible arms are assigned first, then
remaining contacts and arms in stable source/cardinal order. No alternative
trees, axes, poses, or cost-ranked recipes are enumerated.

Port sides derive from the already selected wiring arm or intrinsic incident
direction, then the scope's leading side if undetermined: left for horizontal,
top for vertical. Horizontal Ports default their load downward; vertical Ports
default it rightward. An explicit pose is never reselected to avoid obstacles.
Public boundary sides resolve from explicit settings or parent arms before
child measurement. Default attachment order is first-incidence order from
structural declarations and public attachments, with real contact keys
deduplicated; `.tap()` creation order is not a separate placement instruction.
Applicable explicit `tap_order` supplies a presentation precedence overlay
for otherwise-Default arm assignment and constructive contact placement.
The immutable source attachment inventory keeps its original order;
manual or fixed wiring is not rewritten.
All explicit settings conjoin without silently overwriting each other.

The default reading grammar is local and mechanical. Direct scope peers follow
author declaration order on the scope's horizontal default axis; this does not
require top-aligned child boxes. A root series defaults horizontal. A single
series reads start-to-end horizontally. Every parallel group instead defaults
to a vertical electrical path: its shared start is above its shared end, and
branches are placed left-to-right in declaration order. A `HORIZONTAL` axis
hint on that `ParallelRef` rotates the group to horizontal paths stacked
top-to-bottom. A scope-axis hint changes only the scope's peer arrangement; it
does not silently rotate a parallel group inside that scope. Members inside a
parallel branch follow the parallel group's axis. Grounded ends and glyphs
prefer outward and below their local block, and a branch departs its explicitly
declared through-bus toward its endpoint block. A hint never reverses
electrical pins, series members, or ordered terminals. Source order is a
reading convention, never inferred physical signal, energy, or current flow.

Each Subsystem is recursively expanded into native child structure inside a
measured ownership region with a visible boundary, header, and ID. Theme owns
its presentation colors; color alone never establishes ownership. A reusable
Composite uses the same visible native expansion, because encapsulation limits
user access rather than evidence.

After directions and attachment identities are resolved, each child owns one
fully measured native scene with final frame, public anchors, upright labels,
local grounds, coupling, and reserved exits. Frame and anchors are finalized
together. The frame reserves only actually needed fixed route lanes per side
plus measured labels, title,
ground, border, and escape space; it has no unused full-ring reserve or
redundant straight-connector spacing. This is measurement, not post-hoc cropping,
global clearance reduction, search, or a public coordinate control. The parent
translates that whole payload without relocating measured anchors or rewriting
private contents.
Complete Composite orientation retains its local-frame and inverse-frame
rules. Connected single-pin and genuinely open boundaries remain distinct;
layout never invents a pin, Port, or load.

The authoring projection is a conventional circuit schematic, not an operator
debug view. It does not print `S:`, `P:`, `LINK:`, or `REGION:` marks, routing
guides, or private aliases over the circuit. Its public analysis labels are
exactly the named root Buses and the analysis Coordinates that a child
explicitly publishes with `expose_coordinate()`. Anonymous root Buses,
child-private Buses, anonymous internal identities, Pin/Branch exposures, and
unpublished Coordinates are not labelled. Publishing a Coordinate does not
grant a parent access to private built-Composite handles or create a new
electrical node, Coordinate, attachment arm, wiring permission, or connectivity.
Source aliases remain distinct authored names even when they share conductive
ink. Co-located public aliases are combined into one measured multi-line text
run with each exact name on its own line; a single name containing a literal
middle dot therefore remains distinct from two aliases. The producer retains
different owner-local source groups instead of merging them merely because
compilation gives them one `final_net`.

Analysis labels are measured with the wire Blocks they annotate before final
child frames, public anchors, route lanes, and parent placement are fixed. They
remain visible regardless of `show_parameter_values` and `show_provenance`;
those switches control values and the optional provenance footer, not public
names. Label leaders are nonconductive and do not participate in witness-A
connectivity. The audit verifies the exact captured names and owner scope and
that the leader endpoint is attached to the corresponding conductive-root net,
without treating the text as electrical evidence. It does not independently
distinguish a label swap between different owner-local contacts that share both
scope and electrical net; complete owner-local grouping remains verified source
evidence and a producer invariant.

Native symbols, conductive wires,
filled connection marks, hollow logical-Port endpoints, local grounds, physical
coupling marks, short authored labels, and measured ownership regions carry
the visible meaning. A `NodeMark` label is optional in the authoring projection;
compiled markers that require a label retain it. A harmless filled dot may mark
a connected two-ray bend or contact, while every true three-or-more-ray wire
junction requires a visible dot. An isolated dot or a mark that falsely joins
different nets fails correspondence; this rule does not require every dot to
have three rays. Mutual winding dots are distinct from conductive connection
marks and retain their orientation evidence. A one-pin child boundary may be
one continuous unlabelled wire crossing; a multi-pin boundary retains the local
names needed to distinguish its pins, without a `pin:` type prefix.

Ordinary L and JJ bodies in the normal schematic need neither direction arrows
nor `+`/`−` reference-polarity signs. Their ordered model endpoints and branch
reference conventions remain intact; an unmarked symmetric symbol does not
make that order visible. Mutual couplings retain sufficient visible winding
dots, endpoint incidence, and coupling information to establish relative
polarity. Any presentation of a signed branch current, voltage, or phase must
explain its reference endpoints; this responsibility does not add a signed-result
API or imply that such quantities are available from diagram rendering.

Layout measures native/operator Blocks and complete child regions first, then
jointly places whole Blocks, attachment anchors, and local junctions. A
single-pin readout can hang from a parent tee without adding a second pin or
changing its authoring declaration. A parent moves each child as one unit,
never rewrites its private internals, and attaches connector structures only
at authored endpoints and registered public anchors.
Independent peers follow declaration order or one complete explicit order.
Buses and links are conductive routing demands, not component slots or
pairwise-clique generators. Root Ports stay on their root buses, parent-owned
shunts stay in the parent region, and scopes containing only native peers remain
valid without an invented child or global neighbor partition.

Placement preallocates measured Block, junction-subtree, Port/load/text,
connector, and nonconductive coupling-guide strips. Scope order controls
projected peer order; branch extents may offset rows and enlarge following
columns rather than forcing top-aligned boxes and adding late detours. Each
body is placed once by a stable spanning traversal. The traversal is only a
placement device: every remaining edge or cycle is retained exactly once in
reserved closure tracks.

Channels and distinct lanes are allocated in stable group/connection order
before wire emission. Aligned routes are direct; prescribed bends and
channel/perimeter routes are constructed arithmetically. No visibility graph,
Dijkstra, candidate positions, beam/backtracking, routing-order retries, or
readability score is reachable on the authoring path, including structural
wires, boundary/label completion, and coupling guides. This is constructive
geometry, not a search restricted to one candidate. Different-net crossings
retain the existing jump convention. Separate same-net routes cannot create
incidental bridges, add/erase T/Cross arms, or drop loop edges. Unsupported
fixed geometry fails explicitly, with no alternative search or partial result.

The geometry uses the current renderer revision's uniform `U = 2.2` local
metric, measured text bounds, registered anchors, collision obstacles,
continuous same-net wires, true T junctions, and jump arcs only for
different-net crossings. `U = 2.2` is an implementation setting for that
revision, not a TARGET semantic threshold or a user Gate. Name and value labels
remain separate and readable at the retained minimum scale. Ownership regions,
labels, and any necessary physical-coupling guides are visibly nonconductive.
The light Theme uses a white background, dark conventional ink, and subtle blue
rounded child regions; the dark Theme uses the corresponding readable palette.
Neither Theme changes geometry or evidence. The existing
`show_provenance=True` default shows a compact, separated provenance footer;
setting it to `False` hides only that optional footer. The main circuit remains
readable in either case.

For the no-hint Chapter 1 circuit, these rules produce one readable native
schematic: a hollow Port endpoint reaches a short signal lead and filled T; the
Port-owned reference-impedance load descends from that T to a local ground. A
horizontal coupling capacitor leads to the child resonator. Inside its titled
region, the capacitor and inductor are vertical side-by-side branches between
continuous common top and bottom wires, with one local ground. The Port ground
and resonator ground are separate local glyphs for the same canonical
electrical reference. This public circuit shape is a normative layout case,
not a name-specific renderer rule or a hand-positioned output. Its literal
authored local IDs remain `resonator`, `coupling_cap`, `capacitor`, and
`inductor`; the projection neither title-cases them nor invents aliases such as
`Cc` or `Cr`.

The target does not promise a universal graph-layout algorithm. A failure names
the scope or declared constraints that could not be placed. It returns no
partial or best-effort certified diagram and does not invent retry, drawing-size,
threshold, or time knobs.

## Independent certification {#independent-certification}

One immutable diagram certificate carries expected and independently observed
evidence. The neutral scene cannot contain hidden answer tables that let a
witness copy the expected result. Composition settings and expected ownership
maps are not hidden answers in `NeutralScene`. Separate layout-constraint
verification compares requested shapes and sides against actual visible
geometry; witnesses A/B continue to reconstruct electrical and ownership ink
against the existing Plan/effective-point evidence.

### Electrical witness A

Witness A reconstructs visible component bodies, terminal incidence, wires,
junctions, grounds, Ports, couplings, and compiled matrix associations. For an
authoring projection it compares that reconstruction with the exact complete
Plan at the resolved effective parameter point. For a compiled projection it
compares with the exact compiler-emitted expansion for that same Plan and
point. Identity or correspondence mismatch fails.

For an unmarked ordinary symmetric two-terminal body, including L and JJ,
witness A may compare electrical evidence modulo endpoint-reference reversal.
It cannot independently observe ordered endpoints from that symbol, infer them
from hidden placement or expected metadata, or claim that absence of polarity
signs is an audit failure. Complete ordered model orientation remains separately
verified source/provenance evidence. For mutually coupled branches, A instead
reconstructs relative polarity from actual visible winding dots, their endpoint
incidence, and coupling information. Comparison permits consistent reference
reversal only with the corresponding coupling-sign transformation; it never
drops signed mutual evidence or substitutes hidden orientation for visible
evidence. Required oriented compiled evidence remains unchanged.

With parameter values shown, mutual coupling has a visible signed numerical
coefficient. With `show_parameter_values=False`, its magnitude is hidden and
remains source-verified, while sign-only coupling information (negative,
positive, or zero) and visible dot/incidence evidence remain. A observes the
coupling sign in both modes and the magnitude only when shown.

In authoring projections with `show_parameter_values=True`, witness A
also reconstructs every displayed
effective scalar physical value and its displayed unit, then compares both with
the deterministic six-significant-digit display projection of that resolved
point. This is exact comparison of displayed text/value and units within the
display projection, not a numerical tolerance or a bit-exact Float64 roundtrip
claim. The audit exposes displayed values separately from exact source values.
When value labels are hidden, the scene makes no
visible-scalar-label claim, but the certificate still binds the exact effective
point. This presentation choice does not weaken the compiled projection's
required matrix, coefficient, sign, unit, half-shunt, or omission evidence.

Open public-pin stubs are observed from real visible geometry and terminal
incidence, not open flags, expected maps, or placement records. Partly or
entirely open public interfaces retain their actual boundaries. A cut required
connection is still missing electrical evidence; it cannot be relabelled as a
legal open stub.

Source validation separately proves every exposed Pin's binding to its authored
Bus or Tap. Witness B checks only observable region containment, child-boundary
crossings, and actual inside/outside wire contacts. It does not require a hidden
`bound => visible connected` implication. A straight free-ending exterior
stub on a named root Bus is valid visible ink when no external physical body or
Port was authored there; it is not reclassified as an open child boundary.
Conversely, omitting a genuinely authored external physical, Port, or boundary
connection still fails the applicable source check or visible A/B comparison.

This certifies projection correspondence only. It can detect a drawing or
projection-lowering mismatch, but it does not independently prove numerical
compiler lowering or stamping, a View/PTC realization, or solver correctness.
A correctly drawn yet numerically wrong compiler expansion can pass A/B;
Calculation validates compiler correctness separately. The observed witness
still reconstructs the visible evidence independently rather than copying an
expected manifest.

### Structural witness B

Witness B reconstructs visible:

- recursive visible Subsystem and Composite regions, headers, and containment;
- each visible native leaf's and Port's owning region;
- cross-boundary electrical incidence at visible boundary sites.

Every native leaf's complete occupied symbol-and-label geometry lies in its
owning region and outside child regions, except registered electrical crossings
at child boundaries. For a single unlabelled crossing, witness B checks the
visible wire incidence through the visible boundary; the hidden `PinRef`
identity remains source evidence rather than an observed fact. The undrawn root
scene envelope supplies bounds only and is not an observed B ownership region.
Witness B reads its facts from child-region geometry, headers, native bodies,
Port shapes, and boundary crossings. It does not reconstruct invisible
operator IDs, N-link invocation history, bus or tap names, or coordinate,
branch, and pin-exposure names from the image. It also does not infer or certify
the superseded S/P/M neighbor partition.

Public analysis-name correspondence is a separate text-and-leader observation,
not a hidden Witness-B connectivity answer. It records each exact visible name,
its captured owner scope, and the conductive-root net attached at the leader
endpoint. Multi-line text at one source group does not combine distinct
owner-local groups, and neither the label text nor a shared `final_net` can
supply missing conductive incidence. When distinct contacts in the same scope
share that net, the observation does not claim to recover which contact carried
which name independently of the source record.

The complete authored series, parallel, branch, link, coupling, bus, tap,
grounding, exposure, alias, parameter-definition, parameter-binding,
effective-point, unit, ground-provenance, and ownership records remain
separately available as verified source/provenance rows. They are not Witness B
observations and are never copied into neutral-scene tags as answers.
`audit.show()` labels observed electrical A, observed visible-ownership B,
visible-value checks, and captured source/provenance as distinct evidence
classes.

### Human review C

Human review decides whether the explicit Plan is the intended circuit. A/B
correspondence, hashes, passing layout, and numerical execution cannot make
that design decision.

### Evidence table and digests

The review surface distinguishes observations from verified source facts. It
retains:

- Plan and catalog provenance;
- baseline and selected parameter values, Plan-specific physical consumers,
  and source units;
- Net/BOM and ordered pin/branch tables;
- independently derived expected-visible and observed electrical/structural
  manifests for Witnesses A and B;
- complete verified source rows for authored operators, exposures, parameters,
  buses, taps, grounding, ownership, and their provenance;
- `plan_sha256`, `connectivity_sha256`, and `semantic_sha256`;
- compiler lineage and `expanded_graph_sha256` for compiled views; and
- optional `presentation_sha256` for the frozen scene.

Parameterized rendering additionally binds `parameters_sha256` for the
complete effective point after baseline filling. A selected point does not
mutate `plan_sha256`, but value-dependent expanded, omission, numerical, or
presentation identities may change. The visible expected manifest and observed
A/B reconstruction both use the same exact Plan and point. The
`semantic_sha256` remains the identity of the complete captured source meaning;
it is not a claim that the image independently reveals invisible authoring
history.

Diagram-only grouping never removes an authored Link ID or its unordered
member set from structural evidence, and it never hides effective grounded-net
membership or the owner-local grounding role. Only the source-level batching
and tuple order of `ground_pins()` are nonsemantic provenance excluded from
physical and diagram digests.

The connectivity and semantic digests are representation-tagged. The Plan,
compiler-lineage, and expanded-graph identities retain their own existing
encoders. `expanded_graph_sha256` binds `plan_sha256`, `node_order`,
`resolved_bindings`, and `expanded_branch_rows`; it does not claim that every
solver stamp matrix is independently covered.

`presentation_sha256` excludes its own provenance annotation from the
canonical preimage. It is a reproducible presentation identity, not an
authenticity or security signature. Hiding provenance for publication changes
presentation only; the hidden band cannot be the sole code-free acceptance
packet.

## Compiled matrix-stamp projection {#compiled-projection}

A compiled transmission-line projection preserves the complete matrix-stamp
expansion rather than replacing it with a scalar-equivalent circuit. The
canonical equations, half-shunt handling, coefficient interpretation, and
required visible evidence remain in
[the compiled matrix-stamp implementation](../implementation/results-reports-and-diagrams.qmd#compiled-matrix-stamp-projection).
This contract owns only how that exact emitted expansion is projected and
independently checked for correspondence.

The compiler remains a trusted numerical baseline outside A/B correspondence.
A successful diagram audits its actual effective-point binding and visible
selected values. It does not prove compiler stamping or solver correctness,
unrelated calculation/request overrides, a View/PTC realization, or
optimization correctness.

## Result and presentation boundary {#diagram-result}

Successful rendering returns one immutable `CircuitDiagramResult`. Its
`show()` returns a real Schemdraw `Drawing` through the supported read-only
facade. The existing `Drawing.save()` remains the static-file API; this target
adds no second save/export surface.

For authoring diagrams, `diagram.composition` is an immutable detached public
final recipe. For compiled diagrams it is `None`. Its `show()` remains usable
after the live Plan changes. It exposes neither the internal
`CapturedComposition`/snapshot nor live authoring handles or private editable
contents. `diagram.composition.to_composition(plan=plan)` checks the exact
captured Plan identity and creates a new editable fixed recipe: all resolved
Default-completed public choices become fixed, while hidden internals remain
nonaddressable. Reusing it at another single parameter point remeasures and
reroutes rather than freezing pixels, and may fail if incompatible. There is
no reset-to-auto operation; create a fresh partial composition for new settings.
This adds no request, schema, or digest system.

Theme styling, Notebook zoom/pan/copy controls, and static fallback serialize
the same frozen checked scene. They cannot mutate it, invalidate the
certificate silently, or alter Plan, request, compiler, or Result identity.
Changing layout or Theme may change `presentation_sha256` while Plan,
connectivity, and semantic identities remain fixed for the same exact Plan,
complete effective parameter point, and representation. No invariance is
promised across changed parameter values.

Diagram rendering performs no simulation, allocates no `CircuitRun` workspace,
and creates no solver receipt. A screenshot or zero-output Notebook is
presentation, not certification or scientific evidence.

## Fail-closed behavior {#authoring-diagram-failures}

Assembly failures and editable-state atomicity are defined by the
[assembly contract](circuit-plan-assembly.qmd#assembly-failures).

Rendering returns no `CircuitDiagramResult` when:

- a composition is stale, has an incomplete explicit wiring replacement, or
  contains duplicate, foreign, dead, or conflicting attachments, arms,
  settings, or refs;
- a `SchematicLayout` contains missing, duplicate, foreign, dead, incomplete,
  or conflicting refs;
- a replacement group is grounded, disconnected, or does not cover its complete
  inventory exactly once; or its requested shape/sides disagree with visible
  geometry, including two Ts substituted for a requested Cross;
- required structures, labels, anchors, regions, or wires cannot be placed
  without collision or illegal crossing; or
- the selected deterministic local strategy produces no valid scene.

Those failures use `stage="schematic_layout"`. A mismatch between expected and
independently reconstructed electrical/structural evidence uses
`stage="schematic_audit"`. Neither creates a solver attempt, workspace,
receipt, or partial image.

Invalid types, permissions, stale refs, incomplete replacement wiring, and
other invalid input fail directly. Unsupported fixed geometry reports the
actual scope, Block, junction, or constraint without fallback search or partial
success. It does not label the circuit itself invalid or prove that no other
layout exists. Programming, protocol, and audit-integrity failures propagate.
No elapsed-time threshold or public timeout is part of this contract.

## Tutorial realization {#tutorial-realization}

The canonical Tutorial files are QMD-first TARGET Chapter containers with
generated, zero-output Jupyter artifacts. Short Lessons inside a Chapter may
use its preceding state; every Chapter remains complete from a clean kernel.
The zero-output Notebooks are transport artifacts, not execution records.
Selected checkpoints, including Chapter 1, have genuine source-bound ASCDLS
authoring exports from the assembled Plan and existing render/show/audit path.
The [central evidence status](index.qmd#implementation-evidence-status) and
[figure inventory](../../examples/README.md) distinguish these exports from
whole-course execution and compiled-projection evidence.

| Chapter | Target authoring contribution |
|---|---|
| 1 | fixed-value inline grounded parallel LC, public pin, root coupling and Port, then diagram A/B/C review |
| 2–3 | the complete fixed-value declaration followed by Direct response and retained-node quantity questions |
| 4 | independent definitions, physical-field Plan binding, one selected point, and parameterized diagram evidence |
| 5 | Cartesian and listed parameter spaces, exact point outcomes, selection, and read-only collection |
| 6–7 | the complete parameterized declaration, optimization, report, and exact restart/resolve |
| 8 | project-owned Library |
| 9 | a complete reusable `CompositePlan` factory using the same structure grammar |
| 10 | that complete factory declaration and its public Composite boundary inside another Plan |
| 11 | automatic and handle-based hinted diagrams, one N-endpoint direct stitch, and parent-applied grounding |
| 12 | complete N=2 matrix line, named-tap N=1 feedline, then one whole-RLGC selected-point compiled diagram |
| 13 | one complete Chapter-local parameter-bound feedline/readout/floating capstone, its Plan diagram, then explicit probe PTC |
| 14 | the complete model followed by PTC, pair transform, and retain using public handles |
| 15 | the complete model followed by pump-off HB execution and exact restart/resolve routes |
| 16 | the complete model followed by independent-grid Direct/HB presentation |

Every Chapter is self-contained: it repeats all imports, physical declarations,
and direct handles needed to follow that Chapter from a fresh kernel. Its short
Lessons may share state in order, but no Chapter depends on an included builder,
a Python fixture, or state from another Notebook. This deliberate teaching
repetition does not duplicate contract authority; the declarations apply this
one target grammar.

Across the course, short TARGET cases distinguish intrinsic grounding,
parent-applied grounding, and Port loads; show two independent public returns
grounded to the one reference; and make rejected hierarchy, transitive-bus,
terminal-short, and grounded-Port attempts visible. A caught
authoring failure is followed by a corrected declaration that reuses the
rejected ID, demonstrating atomic failure rather than a partially mutated Plan.

The course always completes the authored model before choosing an analysis
question. ASCDLS translates the explicit Plan into an authoring or compiled
diagram and independently audits that projection. `CircuitRun` separately
supplies `run.original` and any selected analysis View. Rendering may project
one explicit parameter point, but it neither creates nor displays PTC,
transformed/retained coordinates, a parameter space, solver state, or an
analysis `Result`. Successful audited rendering returns the
`CircuitDiagramResult` defined above.

The historical dev5/dev6 numerical meanings remain intact in their renumbered
Chapters 12–16.
Scoped execution evidence does not establish whole-course coverage or Human
acceptance.

## Honest limits and supersession {#honest-limits}

- This document is a `CONVERGING` contract with an integrated implementation
  baseline, not Human acceptance, stabilization, release, or scientific-result
  evidence.
- Durable tests for reopened semantics wait for Human acceptance; current
  evidence limitations are centralized in the Contract map.
- Superseded flat public authoring and catalog-hint APIs are historical
  evidence, not reachable compatibility authorities.
- This target has no public generic netlist-to-intent inference, no
  `SchematicCatalog`, no Participant/Interface/Attachment refs, no S/P/M
  relation API, and no raw coordinate override.
- It does not promise automatic layout for every circuit, infer physical flow,
  or turn diagram success into a product/scientific Gate.
- It does not certify a consumer Design Target, measurement, solver accuracy,
  optimization, PTC, transformed View, or Human intent.
